lines.text: The ditch takes both our fields if it takes either. I wish the stone between us understood that.
I can tell which row you walked by the clay on your boots. The lower end needs a drain.
My father waited for swallows before sowing. He was wrong three years in five, but never stopped saying it.
I have seed enough for the field. Having enough left for supper troubles me.
The buyer says the grain is damp. Yesterday he said the road was dry. It is always weather when he names the price.
The reeve counted my purse twice. I thought of asking whether he expected it to breed.
The ox knows when I am angry. He stands still and lets me use up the words.
A full ditch is a fine thing until it climbs the doorstep.
Give me a plain no before a kind answer that never comes with a spade.
A stone is easy to move. A name in this village takes longer.
The little one asked why the chest has a lock. I said mice. It was an easier answer.
I want one winter with a sound roof and dry lower beds. The court can keep its titles.
I remember who came when the water rose. I remember who stood at the gate as well.
Sometimes I work the last row after dark. Nobody can ask me for anything there.
Tell the child where the ditch runs. We leave enough quarrels without leaving that one.
Tell me what stays in the chest before you tell me what the buyer offered.
Sit while the fire is awake. The field has had your whole day.
I can love you and think you have done a cruel thing. Do not ask me to choose which is true.
I do not need a fine promise. I need to know which words I can build the winter around.
I counted the grain again. I knew the number before opening the lid.
The first warm night smells like a year that might forgive us.
Our neighbour has a hungry house too. That does not make the boundary theirs.
The mending is work even when nobody brings a purse home for it.
Gold buys bread until the road closes. Grain is here already.
Tell me what you want from this life. I would rather hear an unfinished answer than borrow one for you.
I picture the reeve walking past our door without stopping. I do not know what I would do with the silence.
Children hear more through a shutter than grown people think. Let them hear us speak kindly tonight.
I remember what you put aside when you wanted something badly. So do you.
If you see the sea, bring me a stone worn smooth by it. I want to hold the edge of the world.
The house has changed us. I would like us to have some say in what it changes us into.
